identity.name: compute_parcel_cost_estimates
identity.description: Single-phase ENRICHER: streams every residential parcel (zoning_class LIKE 'R%') through the pure pricing engine (scripts/lib/parcel-cost.js) and writes a 13-line renovation-cost menu (JSONB) + 12 headline cost scalars + 3 FSI scalars, one JS-streamed cursor-batched post_commit phase, each batch flushed through its own short transaction. PURE PARCEL MODEL — external industry cost only (archetype_cost_rates); no permit data, no declared cost, no Liar's Gate (Spec 88 §1). CPCE-A1 RULED (Spec 124 R-AR.1): the Phase-B-B3 run-ledger gate is RETIRED as a mechanism — this ENRICHER's runner shape has no gated-skip branch and this step has no lineage-stamp column to hold a Layer-2 predicate; every invocation streams the whole declared population and the 16-column IS DISTINCT FROM write guard keeps a steady-state re-run's write count near zero.

why_lock.text: Spec 47 §A.5 — lock 88 (the owning spec number) is taken by classify-permits.js (predates the spec-number convention); 117 is the assigned free-ID from the post-Wave-7 range, ported verbatim from the pre-conversion `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 117` and agreeing with pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts:143. O1 CORRECTION (2026-09-21): this sentence previously (falsely) claimed the audit_table `phase` key still carries the spec number (88) — it does not; see `sharing.varies_by_chain.phase.sources` and the deviations[] entry below for the actual (fleet-standard) value.

guard_columns_why.text: The verbatim 16-column guard, legacy `distinctGuard = ['parcel_cost_menu', ...ALL_SCALAR_COLS]`. All 16 are in the guard — the mechanism that makes a re-run against unchanged inputs write ~0 rows instead of re-pricing 437,279 parcels every invocation (measured live: 77/190 of 437,281 candidates on the two July ledger rows).

write_discipline.scope: p.zoning_class IS NOT NULL AND upper(p.zoning_class) LIKE 'R%' (CPCE-A6 RULED — a population definition, not a threshold)

guard_columns_why.text: CPCE-D2 CLOSED. The SAME 16-column set as writes[0]'s guard, OR-joined by write.js's set-based codegen — "carries at least one of the 16 cost/FSI values" is the predicate that confines the retraction to a parcel that genuinely has something to null, so a parcel already all-NULL (never priced, or already retracted by a prior run) is never rewritten. `set_value: null` on all 16 columns is what makes this a class-O (set_based_null_retract) target rather than a per-row value write — the UPDATE ... SET <col> = NULL ... WHERE <scope> AND (<16 guards OR-joined>) shape write.js#buildWritePlan already generates for `set_based_null_retract`.

idempotent_rerun_why.text: CPCE-D2 CLOSED, WIDENED S0.2 — still self-extinguishing (the geocode_permits zombie-cleanup precedent's own idempotent_rerun_why shape). After the retraction fires, the row's 16 cost/FSI columns are NULL, so the guard ("at least one IS DISTINCT FROM NULL") excludes it on every subsequent run — the SAME row can never be retracted twice. The scope itself is a pure population predicate (independent of whether cost columns are set), so a full re-run's before-image SELECT still reads every row matching the WIDENED scope (non-R% OR (R% AND out-of-product-scope) — S0.2 measured 18,529 additional R%-scoped rows on top of CPCE-D2's original 49,251 non-R% population) even though the guarded UPDATE changes 0 rows after convergence — declared here rather than left as a silent cost: the retraction is cheap (0 rows changed at steady state), the before-image SELECT is not scope-narrowed by the guard (write.js#buildBeforeImageSelectSql reads plan.scope only, the SAME declared divergence geocode_permits' writes[1] documents). Filed MED in review_followups.md; not a correctness defect.

why.text: CPCE-D2 CLOSED (Spec 88 §2.1/§2.10), WIDENED by S0.2 (WF3 existing-structure-area-artifacts, 2026-09-21/22) — the SAME retraction target, widened rather than duplicated (FOLD-I1: 'NEVER a second code path'). ORIGINAL (CPCE-D2): a parcel re-zoned OUT of the R% population after `writes[0]` priced it keeps its stale menu + 15 scalars forever. Measured live 2026-09-21: 2 parcels (373779 CR, 11891 O). NEW (S0.2): `tasks/lessons.md:30` — enrich_parcels' max-build pass had ALREADY ruled 18,529 R%-scoped parcels out of the product model (`max_buildable_gfa_sqm IS NULL` — lot outside `[max_build_lot_min_sqm, max_build_lot_max_sqm]`, S0.1) or beyond the residual existing-GFA cut (`cur_floor_gfa_sqm > product_scope_max_existing_gfa_sqm`, FOLD-RC2) while `writes[0]` priced their reno lines anyway — $77,593,312,011.51 of `cost_gut_total` alone (12.96% of the whole population's Σ), including 103 of 103 parcels above $50M. `buildSourceSql` (the forward pricing stream) carries the SAME bound so a newly-excluded parcel is never re-priced in the same run the retraction just cleaned it in. Widening the population (pricing genuinely out-of-model parcels) was refused (Spec 88 §1 scopes the model to residential, IN-MODEL parcels); leave-and-flag was refused (Spec 124 §7's NEVER clause).

recovery.reset: No TRUNCATE/rebuild mechanism and none is needed — a plain re-run re-streams the whole R% population (staleness.scope 'all') and the 16-column IS DISTINCT FROM guard makes an unnecessary re-write cheap.

interrupted_why.text: Unlike a shared-txn ENRICHER, this step has NO shared transaction (`execution.txn_scope:"none"`) — each ctx.flushBatch call is its OWN short transaction, so a run killed mid-stream leaves already-flushed batches COMMITTED (execution.partial_fill:"staged"). 'none' is the honest recovery value (no special action needed), NOT `force_full_on_next_run`: staleness.scope is unconditionally 'all' already, so the very next run re-streams and re-prices every row regardless of whether the prior run was interrupted, converging without any special-cased recovery branch. Proven by the new compute-parcel-cost-kill-mid-run.db.test.ts (pg_cancel_backend, not a process kill).
